   864	    async fn run_state_machine(&mut self) -> Result<WorkerState> {
   865	        loop {
   866	            // Check for shutdown signal between states.
   867	            if self.shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
   868	                // Retrieve and clear the last received signal for logging.
   869	                #[cfg(unix)]
   870	                let signal_name = {
   871	                    let sig = LAST_SIGNAL.swap(0, AtomicOrdering::SeqCst);
   872	                    if sig == 0 {
   873	                        None
   874	                    } else {
   875	                        Some(match sig {
   876	                            1 => "SIGHUP",
   877	                            2 => "SIGINT",
   878	                            15 => "SIGTERM",
   879	                            _ => "unknown signal",
   880	                        })
   881	                    }
   882	                };
   883	                #[cfg(not(unix))]
   884	                let signal_name = None;
   885	
   886	                let reason = if let Some(name) = signal_name {
   887	                    format!("signal received ({name})")
   888	                } else {
   889	                    "signal received".to_string()
   890	                };
   891	
   892	                match self.state {
   893	                    // If we're in the middle of processing a bead, release it
   894	                    // before stopping. This ensures the bead is returned to
   895	                    // the open state and can be claimed by another worker.
   896	                    WorkerState::Building
   897	                    | WorkerState::Dispatching
   898	                    | WorkerState::Executing
   899	                    | WorkerState::Handling => {
   900	                        // Release any claimed bead before stopping.
   901	                        self.release_current_bead(&reason).await;
   902	                        return self.stop(&reason).await;
   903	                    }
   904	                    // For states where we don't hold a bead, stop immediately.
   905	                    WorkerState::Selecting
   906	                    | WorkerState::Claiming
   907	                    | WorkerState::Retrying
   908	                    | WorkerState::Logging => {
   909	                        // Release any claimed bead before stopping (should be none in these states).
   910	                        self.release_current_bead(&reason).await;
   911	                        return self.stop(&reason).await;
   912	                    }
   913	                    WorkerState::Stopped | WorkerState::Exhausted | WorkerState::Errored => {
   914	                        return self.stop(&reason).await;
   915	                    }
   916	                    WorkerState::Booting => {
   917	                        return self.stop("signal received during boot").await;
   918	                    }
   919	                }
   920	            }
   921	
   922	            // Check for watchdog trigger - this indicates HANDLING state is wedged.
   923	            // The watchdog runs in a separate thread and can detect when the worker
   924	            // is stuck even if the Tokio runtime becomes unresponsive.
   925	            if self.watchdog_triggered.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
   926	                && self.state == WorkerState::Handling
   927	            {
   928	                tracing::error!("watchdog detected HANDLING state hang, forcing recovery");
   929	                // Emit critical timeout event.
   930	                let bead_id = self.current_bead.as_ref().map(|b| b.id.clone());
   931	                let _ = self
   932	                    .telemetry
   933	                    .emit_try_lock(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {
   934	                        bead_id: bead_id.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| BeadId::from("unknown")),
   935	                        outcome: "unknown".to_string(),
   936	                        operation: "watchdog".to_string(),
   937	                        error: format!(
   938	                            "HANDLING state exceeded {}s timeout",
   939	                            HANDLING_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_SECS
   940	                        ),
   941	                    });
   942	                // Attempt best-effort release if we have a bead.
   943	                if let Some(ref bead) = self.current_bead {
   944	                    let bead_id = bead.id.clone();
   945	                    tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead_id, "best-effort bead release due to watchdog timeout");
   946	                    let _ =
   947	                        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(30), self.store.release(&bead_id))
   948	                            .await;
   949	                }
   950	                // Clear the watchdog trigger and force transition to LOGGING.
   951	                self.watchdog_triggered.store(false, Ordering::Release);
   952	                self.handling_state_entered_at = None;
   953	                // Force transition to LOGGING to recover.
   954	                self.set_state(WorkerState::Logging)?;
   955	            }
   956	
   957	            // A plain `Span` handle is safe to clone and move between threads. Each
   958	            // bead-processing handler is instrumented separately so its polls and
   959	            // synchronous tracing events see the lifecycle span as current without
   960	            // keeping a thread-local entry alive between polls.
   961	            let lifecycle_span = self
   962	                .bead_lifecycle_span
   963	                .clone()
   964	                .unwrap_or_else(tracing::Span::none);
   965	
   966	            match self.state {
   967	                WorkerState::Selecting => self.do_select().await?,
   968	                WorkerState::Claiming => self.do_claim().await?,
   969	                WorkerState::Retrying => self.do_retry().await?,
   970	                WorkerState::Building => self.do_build().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?,
   971	                WorkerState::Dispatching => {
   972	                    self.do_dispatch()
   973	                        .instrument(lifecycle_span.clone())
   974	                        .await?
   975	                }
   976	                WorkerState::Executing => {
   977	                    self.do_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?
   978	                }
   979	                WorkerState::Handling => {
   980	                    self.do_handle().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?
   981	                }
   982	                WorkerState::Logging => {
   983	                    lifecycle_span.in_scope(|| self.do_log())?;
   984	
   985	                    // After logging completes, check if the running binary is stale
   986	                    // compared to the latest needle-stable on disk. If a newer binary
   987	                    // is detected, exit cleanly so a supervisor or relaunch can pick
   988	                    // up the new binary. This check runs between dispatch cycles,
   989	                    // never mid-claim, ensuring no bead is left in_progress.
   990	                    if let Err(e) = self.check_hot_reload().await {
   991	                        tracing::warn!(
   992	                            error = %e,
   993	                            "hot-reload check failed, continuing on current binary"
   994	                        );
   995	                    }
   996	                    // If check_hot_reload() detected a new binary and successfully
   997	                    // re-execed, we won't reach here (the process is replaced).
   998	                    // On re-exec failure, we continue normally.
   999	
  1000	                    // After hot-reload check, perform the periodic freshness check.
  1001	                    // This runs at the configured interval (worker.freshness_check_interval_secs)
  1002	                    // and logs warnings when a stale binary is detected, but does NOT exit.
  1003	                    // The distinction: hot-reload exits cleanly when new binary is available;
  1004	                    // freshness checking warns but continues processing.
  1005	                    if let Err(e) = self.check_freshness().await {
  1006	                        tracing::warn!(
  1007	                            error = %e,
  1008	                            "freshness check failed, continuing with current binary"
  1009	                        );
  1010	                    }
  1011	                }
  1012	                WorkerState::Exhausted => {
  1013	                    let next = self.handle_exhausted().await?;
  1014	                    match next {
  1015	                        WorkerState::Selecting => continue,
  1016	                        terminal => return Ok(terminal),
  1017	                    }
  1018	                }
  1019	                WorkerState::Stopped => {
  1020	                    return self.stop("normal shutdown").await;
  1830	            }
  1831	            ClaimResult::Suspect {
  1832	                bead_id,
  1833	                consecutive_errors,
  1834	                last_error,
  1835	            } => {
  1836	                tracing::warn!(
  1837	                    bead_id = %bead_id,
  1838	                    consecutive_errors,
  1839	                    %last_error,
  1840	                    "bead marked as suspect after repeated claim errors"
  1841	                );
  1842	                // Record on claim_span explicitly — see the RaceLost arm.
  1843	                claim_span.record("needle.claim.result", "suspect");
  1844	                claim_span.record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
  1845	                claim_span.record(
  1846	                    "otel.status_description",
  1847	                    format!(
  1848	                        "suspect: {} consecutive errors: {}",
  1849	                        consecutive_errors, last_error
  1850	                    ),
  1851	                );
  1852	                // Emit telemetry for the suspect bead
  1853	                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimErrorThreshold {
  1854	                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
  1855	                    consecutive_errors,
  1856	                    last_error,
  1857	                })?;
  1858	                // Exclude the suspect bead and continue
  1859	                self.consecutive_race_lost = 0;
  1860	                self.exclusion_set.insert(bead_id);
  1861	                self.current_bead = None;
  1862	                // The claim_span is dropped here, closing the bead.claim span.
  1863	                self.set_state(WorkerState::Selecting)?;
  1864	            }
  1865	        }
  1866	
  1867	        Ok(())
  1868	    }
  1869	
  1870	    /// RETRYING: decide whether to retry claiming or move on.
  1871	    ///
  1872	    /// Tracks consecutive race_lost across retry cycles. When the count
  1873	    /// exceeds `claim_race_lost_skip`, the worker treats the ready queue
  1874	    /// as effectively empty and transitions to Exhausted instead of
  1875	    /// spinning indefinitely on the same bead.
  1876	    async fn do_retry(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
  1877	        let skip_threshold = self.config.worker.claim_race_lost_skip;
  1878	
  1879	        if self.consecutive_race_lost >= skip_threshold {
  1880	            tracing::warn!(
  1881	                consecutive_race_lost = self.consecutive_race_lost,
  1882	                threshold = skip_threshold,
  1883	                "consecutive race_lost exceeded skip threshold, treating queue as exhausted"
  1884	            );
  1885	            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimRaceLostSkipped {
  1886	                consecutive_losses: self.consecutive_race_lost,
  1887	                threshold: skip_threshold,
  1888	            })?;
  1889	            self.consecutive_race_lost = 0;
  1890	            self.retry_count = 0;
  1891	            self.exclusion_set.clear();
  1892	            self.race_lost_this_cycle.clear();
  1893	            self.current_bead = None;
  1894	            self.set_state(WorkerState::Exhausted)?;
  1895	            return Ok(());
  1896	        }
  1897	
  1898	        // Exponential backoff: start at 100ms, doubling each time, capped at 5s.
  1899	        // This ensures even the first retry has a small delay to prevent tight loops.
  1900	        let backoff_ms = if self.consecutive_race_lost > 0 {
  1901	            // For race-lost retries: 100ms, 200ms, 400ms, 800ms, 1600ms, 3200ms, 5000ms (capped)
  1902	            std::cmp::min(
  1903	                100 * (1u64 << (self.consecutive_race_lost - 1).min(5)),
  1904	                5000,
  1905	            )
  1906	        } else {
  1907	            // For other retries (e.g., max_claim_retries): 100ms minimum
  1908	            100
  1909	        };
  1910	        tracing::debug!(
  1911	            consecutive_race_lost = self.consecutive_race_lost,
  1912	            backoff_ms,
  1913	            "backing off before retry"
  1914	        );
  1915	        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms)).await;
  1916	
  1917	        if self.retry_count < self.config.worker.max_claim_retries {
  1918	            self.set_state(WorkerState::Selecting)?;
  1919	        } else {
  1920	            tracing::debug!(
  1921	                retry_count = self.retry_count,
  1922	                "max claim retries exceeded, clearing retry state for next cycle"
  1923	            );
  1924	            self.retry_count = 0;
  1925	            self.consecutive_race_lost = 0;
  1926	            self.exclusion_set.clear();
  1927	            self.race_lost_this_cycle.clear();
  1928	            // NOTE: Do NOT clear race_lost_exclusions here. Those have TTL-based
  1929	            // expiration and must persist to prevent re-selecting the same bead
  1930	            // that just lost a claim race. Clearing them would cause an infinite
  1931	            // race-lost loop (see needle-aad8).
  1932	            self.current_bead = None;
  1933	            self.set_state(WorkerState::Selecting)?;
  1934	        }
  1935	        Ok(())
  1936	    }
  1937	
  1938	    /// BUILDING: construct prompt from claimed bead.
  1939	    async fn do_build(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
  1940	        let bead_id = match self.current_bead.as_ref() {
  1941	            Some(bead) => bead.id.clone(),
  1942	            None => bail!("BUILDING state without current_bead — invariant violated"),
  1943	        };
  1944	        let prompt_build_span = tracing::info_span!(
  1945	            "bead.prompt_build",
  1946	            needle.bead.id = %bead_id,
  1947	        );
  1948	
  1949	        self.do_build_inner().instrument(prompt_build_span).await
  1950	    }
  1951	
  1952	    async fn do_build_inner(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
  1953	        let bead = match self.current_bead {
  1954	            Some(ref b) => b.clone(),
  1955	            None => {
  1956	                bail!("BUILDING state without current_bead — invariant violated");
  1957	            }
  1958	        };
  1959	
  1960	        let build_ws = if is_workspace_unset(&bead.workspace) {
  1961	            self.config.workspace.default.clone()
  1962	        } else {
  1963	            bead.workspace.clone()
  1964	        };
  1965	
  1966	        let worker_name = self.worker_name.clone();
  1967	        let prompt_builder = self.prompt_builder.clone();
  1968	
  1969	        // Wrap prompt building in timeout. The build operation can be slow for
  1970	        // large workspaces with many learning files.
  1971	        // Enforce minimum timeout to prevent indefinite hangs (issue needle-3igr).
  1972	        const MIN_BUILDING_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 60;
  1973	        let timeout_secs = self
  1974	            .config
  1975	            .worker
  1976	            .building_timeout
  1977	            .max(MIN_BUILDING_TIMEOUT_SECS);
  1978	        let timeout_dur = std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);
  1979	        let bead_id = bead.id.clone();
  1980	        let heartbeat_bead_id = bead_id.clone();
  1981	        let telemetry = self.telemetry.clone();
  1982	
  1983	        // Spawn heartbeat task that emits periodic updates during the build.
  1984	        // Heartbeat interval: every 30 seconds.
  1985	        let heartbeat_handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
  1986	            let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30));
  1987	            let start = std::time::Instant::now();
  1988	            loop {
  1989	                interval.tick().await;
  1990	                let elapsed_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;
  1991	                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::BuildHeartbeat {
  1992	                    bead_id: heartbeat_bead_id.clone(),
  1993	                    elapsed_ms,
  1994	                });
  1995	            }
  1996	        });
  1997	
  1998	        // Check if we should use SPLIT mode instead of normal PLUCK.
  1999	        // Auto-split triggers when a bead has >= split_after_failures consecutive failures.
  2000	        let (template_name, failure_count) = self.check_split_mode(&bead).await;
  2001	
  2002	        // If SPLIT mode would be used, check if the bead references NEEDLE-internal
  2003	        // configuration. These tasks have no legitimate resolution path from inside
  2004	        // a target repo and should not be split into child beads there.
  2005	        if template_name == "split" && detects_needle_internal_config(&bead) {
  2006	            heartbeat_handle.abort();
  2007	
  2008	            tracing::info!(
  2009	                bead_id = %bead_id,
  2010	                title = %bead.title,
  2011	                failure_count,
  2012	                "SPLIT mode skipped: bead references NEEDLE-internal configuration"
  2013	            );
  2014	
  2015	            // Set Error status on the bead.prompt_build span
  2016	            tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
  2017	            tracing::Span::current().record(
  2018	                "otel.status_description",
  2019	                "skipped: references NEEDLE-internal configuration",
  2020	            );
  2021	
  2022	            // Emit split.skipped event.
  2023	            let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::SplitSkipped {
  2024	                bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
  2025	                reason: "references NEEDLE-internal configuration".to_string(),
  2026	            });
  2027	
  2028	            // Release the bead with timeout protection.
  2029	            let _ = tokio::time::timeout(
  2030	                std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
  2031	                self.store.release(&bead_id),
  2032	            )
  2033	            .await;
  2034	
  2035	            // Emit bead.released event.
  2036	            let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::BeadReleased {
  2037	                bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
  2038	                reason: "split_out_of_scope".to_string(),
  2039	            });
  2040	
  2041	            // Clear current bead and transition to RETRYING.
  2042	            self.current_bead = None;
  2043	            self.set_state(WorkerState::Retrying)?;
  2044	            return Ok(());
  2045	        }
  2046	
  2047	        let mut prompt = match tokio::time::timeout(
  2048	            timeout_dur,
  2049	            tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
  2050	                if template_name == "split" {
  2051	                    prompt_builder.build_split(&bead, &build_ws, &worker_name, failure_count)
  2052	                } else {
  2053	                    prompt_builder.build_pluck(&bead, &build_ws, &worker_name)
  2054	                }
  2055	            }),
  2056	        )
  2057	        .await
  2058	        {
  2059	            Ok(Ok(result)) => result?,
  2060	            Ok(Err(e)) => {
  2061	                heartbeat_handle.abort();
  2062	                bail!("prompt building task failed: {}", e);
  2063	            }
  2064	            Err(_) => {
  2065	                heartbeat_handle.abort();
  2066	                // Timeout: release the bead and transition to RETRYING.
  2067	                tracing::error!(
  2068	                    bead_id = %bead_id,
  2069	                    timeout_secs = timeout_secs,
  2070	                    configured_timeout = self.config.worker.building_timeout,
  2071	                    "BUILDING state timed out"
  2072	                );
  2073	
  2074	                // Set Error status on the bead.prompt_build span
  2075	                tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
  2076	                tracing::Span::current().record(
  2077	                    "otel.status_description",
  2078	                    format!("timeout after {}s", timeout_secs),
  2079	                );
  2080	
  2081	                // Emit build.timeout event.
  2082	                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::BuildTimeout {
  2083	                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
  2084	                    timeout_secs,
  2085	                });
  2086	                crate::hoop_hooks::emit_needle_event(
  2087	                    &self.current_workspace,
  2088	                    &self.worker_name,
  2089	                    Some(bead_id.as_ref()),
  2090	                    self.current_strand.as_deref(),
  2091	                    "timeout",
  2092	                    serde_json::json!({}),
  2093	                );
  2094	
  2095	                // Release the bead with timeout protection.
  2096	                let _ = tokio::time::timeout(
  2097	                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
  2098	                    self.store.release(&bead_id),
  2099	                )
  2100	                .await;
  2101	
  2102	                // Emit bead.released event.
  2103	                let _ = self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::BeadReleased {
  2104	                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
  2105	                    reason: "build_timeout".to_string(),
  2106	                });
  2107	                crate::hoop_hooks::emit_needle_event(
  2108	                    &self.current_workspace,
  2109	                    &self.worker_name,
  2110	                    Some(bead_id.as_ref()),
  2111	                    self.current_strand.as_deref(),
  2112	                    "release",
  2113	                    serde_json::json!({}),
  2114	                );
  2115	
  2116	                // Clear current bead and transition to RETRYING.
  2117	                self.current_bead = None;
  2118	                self.set_state(WorkerState::Retrying)?;
  2119	                return Ok(());
  2120	            }
  2121	        };
  2122	
  2123	        // Stop heartbeat task.
  2124	        heartbeat_handle.abort();
  2125	
  2126	        // Prepend the HOOP dispatch tag so session tailers can join transcripts
  2127	        // back to beads. Format: [needle:<qualified-worker>:<bead-id>:<strand>]
  2128	        let strand = self.current_strand.as_deref().unwrap_or("pluck");
  2129	        prompt.content = format!(
  2130	            "[needle:{}:{}:{}]\n{}",
  2131	            self.qualified_id(),
  2132	            bead_id,
  2133	            strand,
  2134	            prompt.content
  2135	        );
  2136	
  2137	        // Store the prompt for the dispatch phase. We use a transient field pattern:
  2138	        // the prompt is passed via self.built_prompt.
  2139	        self.built_prompt = Some(prompt);
  2140	        self.set_state(WorkerState::Dispatching)?;
  2141	        Ok(())
  2142	    }
  2143	
  2144	    /// DISPATCHING: check rate limits, resolve adapter, and prepare for execution.
  2145	    async fn do_dispatch(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
  2145	    async fn do_dispatch(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
  2146	        if self.current_bead.is_none() {
  2147	            bail!("DISPATCHING state without current_bead — invariant violated");
  2148	        }
  2149	
  2150	        // Check rate limits before dispatching.
  2151	        let adapter = self.resolve_adapter()?;
  2152	        let provider = adapter.provider.as_deref();
  2153	        let model = adapter.model.as_deref();
  2154	        self.health.update_adapter(Some(&adapter.name));
  2155	
  2156	        // Enter the agent.dispatch span for the dispatching phase.
  2157	        let _bead_id = self.current_bead.as_ref().map(|b| b.id.clone());
  2158	        crate::hoop_hooks::emit_needle_event(
  2159	            &self.current_workspace,
  2160	            &self.worker_name,
  2161	            _bead_id.as_ref().map(|id| id.as_ref()),
  2162	            self.current_strand.as_deref(),
  2163	            "dispatch",
  2164	            serde_json::json!({"adapter": adapter.name, "model": model}),
  2165	        );
  2166	        let dispatch_span = tracing::info_span!(
  2167	            "agent.dispatch",
  2168	            gen_ai.system = %provider.unwrap_or("unknown"),
  2169	            gen_ai.request.model = %model.unwrap_or("unknown"),
  2170	            needle.agent.pid = tracing::field::Empty, // Will be set when process starts
  2171	            needle.agent.exit_code = tracing::field::Empty, // Will be set after execution
  2172	        );
  2173	
  2174	        self.do_dispatch_inner(adapter)
  2175	            .instrument(dispatch_span)
  2176	            .await
  2177	    }
  2178	
  2179	    async fn do_dispatch_inner(&mut self, adapter: crate::dispatch::AgentAdapter) -> Result<()> {
  2180	        let provider = adapter.provider.as_deref();
  2181	        let model = adapter.model.as_deref();
  2182	
  2183	        let decision = self.rate_limiter.check(provider, model, &self.registry)?;
  2184	
  2185	        if !decision.is_allowed() {
  2186	            let reason = format!("{decision}");
  2187	            tracing::info!(
  2188	                reason = %reason,
  2189	                "rate limited, waiting before retry"
  2190	            );
  2191	            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::RateLimitWait {
  2192	                provider: provider.unwrap_or("unknown").to_string(),
  2193	                model: model.map(|s| s.to_string()),
  2194	                reason: reason.clone(),
  2195	            })?;
  2196	
  2197	            // Wait before retrying (5 seconds).
  2198	            tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
  2199	
  2200	            // Stay in Dispatching state to retry the rate limit check.
  2201	            return Ok(());
  2202	        }
  2203	
  2204	        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::RateLimitAllowed {
  2205	            provider: provider.unwrap_or("unknown").to_string(),
  2206	            model: model.map(|s| s.to_string()),
  2207	        })?;
  2208	
  2209	        // Check system resources (CPU and memory warnings).
  2210	        crate::rate_limit::RateLimiter::check_system_resources(
  2211	            self.config.worker.cpu_load_warn,
  2212	            self.config.worker.memory_free_warn_mb,
  2213	            &self.telemetry,
  2214	        );
  2215	
  2216	        self.set_state(WorkerState::Executing)?;
  2217	        Ok(())
  2218	    }
  2219	
  2220	    /// EXECUTING: run the agent process and capture output.
  2221	    async fn do_execute(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
  2222	        let bead = match self.current_bead {
  2223	            Some(ref b) => b.clone(),
  2224	            None => {
  2225	                bail!("EXECUTING state without current_bead — invariant violated");
  2226	            }
  2227	        };
  2228	
  2229	        let prompt = match self.built_prompt.take() {
  2230	            Some(p) => p,
  2231	            None => {
  2232	                bail!("EXECUTING state without built_prompt — invariant violated");
  2233	            }
  2234	        };
  2235	
  2236	        let adapter = self.resolve_adapter()?;
  2237	
  2238	        // Use the bead's workspace if set (remote bead from Explore),
  2239	        // otherwise fall back to the config's default workspace.
  2240	        let dispatch_ws = if is_workspace_unset(&bead.workspace) {
  2241	            &self.config.workspace.default
  2242	        } else {
  2243	            &bead.workspace
  2244	        };
  2245	
  2246	        // Race the dispatch against the shutdown signal.
  2247	        let was_interrupted;
  2248	        let exec_result = if self.shutdown.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
  2249	            // Already shutting down — don't start the agent.
  2250	            was_interrupted = true;
  2251	            None
  2252	        } else {
  2253	            // Capture HEAD so do_handle can tag new commits with Bead-Id on success.
  2254	            // Wrap in timeout to prevent indefinite hang if git subprocess hangs.
  2255	            match tokio::time::timeout(
  2256	                std::time::Duration::from_secs(10),
  2257	                commit_hook::git_head(dispatch_ws.to_str().unwrap_or(".")),
  2258	            )
  2259	            .await
  2260	            {
  2261	                Ok(Ok(head)) => {
  2262	                    self.pre_dispatch_head = Some(head);
  2263	                }
  2264	                Ok(Err(e)) => {
  2265	                    tracing::debug!(
  2266	                        workspace = %dispatch_ws.display(),
  2267	                        error = %e,
  2268	                        "git_head failed (not a git repo or git error), skipping Bead-Id trailer"
  2269	                    );
  2270	                }
  2271	                Err(_) => {
  2272	                    tracing::warn!(
  2273	                        workspace = %dispatch_ws.display(),
  2274	                        "git_head timed out after 10s, skipping Bead-Id trailer"
  2275	                    );
  2276	                }
  2277	            }
  2278	            // Enter the agent.execution span for the actual agent process execution.
  2279	            // This is a child of agent.dispatch.
  2280	            // We need to record attributes on the parent agent.dispatch span after execution,
  2281	            // so we use a scope to drop the execution_span guard first.
  2282	            let execution_span = tracing::info_span!(
  2283	                "agent.execution",
  2284	                needle.bead.id = %bead.id,
  2285	            );
  2286	            // Hoisted out of the async block below: qualified_id() is a method
  2287	            // call, so using it inside the coroutine would borrow all of *self and
  2288	            // collide with the mutable use of self.exec_started_at (E0500). A field
  2289	            // access like self.worker_name is a disjoint capture and does not, but
  2290	            // worker_name is the WRONG actor -- the claim is made with qualified_id().
  2291	            let qualified_actor = self.qualified_id();
  2292	            let (result, exec_tokens) = async {
  2293	                // Snapshot workspace HEAD + the bead's notes before the agent
  2294	                // runs, so the shipped-work gate has a baseline to judge the
  2295	                // closure against. Best-effort: a missing snapshot degrades the
  2296	                // gate to its conservative path, it never blocks dispatch.
  2297	                if let Err(e) = crate::validation::predispatch::record(
  2298	                    dispatch_ws,
  2299	                    &bead.id,
  2300	                    self.store.as_ref(),
  2301	                )
  2302	                .await
  2303	                {
  2304	                    tracing::warn!(
  2305	                        bead_id = %bead.id,
  2306	                        error = %e,
  2307	                        "failed to record pre-dispatch snapshot — shipped-work gate will fall back"
  2308	                    );
  2309	                }
  2310	
  2311	                // ── Atomic claim verification at dispatch time ──
  2312	                // Verify that the bead is still assigned to this worker immediately
  2313	                // before dispatch. This prevents double-dispatch where two workers
  2314	                // dispatch the same bead concurrently.
  2315	                //
  2316	                // This check queries the LIVE bead store (not a stale snapshot) to
  2317	                // ensure the bead is still in_progress and assigned to this worker.
  2318	                // If another worker has reassigned the bead or the bead has been
  2319	                // released, we abort the dispatch.
  2320	                let is_valid = self
  2321	                    .claimer
  2322	                    .verify_claim_at_dispatch(&bead.id, &qualified_actor)
  2323	                    .await
  2324	                    .with_context(|| {
  2325	                        format!(
  2326	                            "dispatch-time claim verification failed for bead {}",
  2327	                            bead.id
  2328	                        )
  2329	                    })?;
  2330	
  2331	                if !is_valid {
  2332	                    // Bead is not assigned to this worker - abort dispatch.
  2333	                    // Release the bead back to ready state so another worker can claim it.
  2334	                    tracing::warn!(
  2335	                        bead_id = %bead.id,
  2336	                        worker = %self.worker_name,
  2337	                        "dispatch-time claim verification failed: bead not assigned to this worker, aborting dispatch and releasing back to ready state"
  2338	                    );
  2339	
  2340	                    // Release the bead back to open status
  2341	                    if let Err(e) = self.store.release(&bead.id).await {
  2342	                        tracing::error!(
  2343	                            bead_id = %bead.id,
  2344	                            error = %e,
  2345	                            "failed to release bead after dispatch-time verification failure"
  2346	                        );
  2347	                    }
  2348	
  2349	                    // Emit telemetry for the failed verification

  2459	    /// Creates `.beads/traces/<bead-id>/` directory and writes:

  2465	    fn write_trace_files(
  2466	        &self,
  2467	        bead_id: &crate::types::BeadId,
  2468	        workspace: &std::path::Path,
  2469	        stdout: &str,
  2470	        stderr: &str,

  2473	
  2474	        // Build trace directory path: <workspace>/.beads/traces/<bead-id>/

  2478	            .join(bead_id.as_ref());
  2479

  2482	        fs::create_dir_all(&trace_dir).with_context(|| {

  2485	                trace_dir.display()

  2487	        })?;

  2617	                    tracing::Span::current()
  2618	                        .record("needle.outcome.action", result.bead_action.to_string());
  2619	
  2620	                    // Store outcome for recording on bead.lifecycle span
  2621	                    self.last_outcome = Some(result.outcome.as_str().to_string());
  2622	
  2623	                    // Set span status: Ok for Success, Error for all other outcomes.
  2624	                    match result.outcome {
  2625	                        crate::types::Outcome::Success => {
  2626	                            // Span status is Ok by default
  2627	                        }
  2628	                        _ => {
  2629	                            // Set Error status with the outcome as description
  2630	                            // otel.status_code = 2 indicates ERROR in OpenTelemetry
  2631	                            tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
  2632	                            tracing::Span::current()
  2633	                                .record("otel.status_description", result.outcome.as_str());
  2634	                        }
  2635	                    }
  2636	
  2637	                    tracing::debug!(
  2638	                        bead_id = %bead.id,
  2639	                        outcome = %result.outcome,
  2640	                        action = %result.bead_action,
  2641	                        "handler completed successfully, stopping heartbeat task"
  2642	                    );
  2643	                    Ok(result)
  2644	                }
  2645	                Ok(Err(e)) => {
  2646	                    // Handler returned an error - attempt best-effort release and recover.
  2647	                    tracing::error!(
  2648	                        bead_id = %bead.id,
  2649	                        error = %e,
  2650	                        "outcome handler failed, attempting best-effort release and transitioning to LOGGING"
  2651	                    );
  2652	                    // Set cancellation flag to stop heartbeat and abort any in-flight br calls.
  2653	                    cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);
  2654	                    // Abort the heartbeat task to prevent it from continuing in the background.
  2655	                    heartbeat_task.abort();
  2656	                    // Use emit_try_lock() to avoid blocking on telemetry mutex if writer is stuck.
  2657	                    let _ = telemetry_clone.emit_try_lock(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {
  2658	                        bead_id: bead_id_clone.clone(),
  2659	                        outcome: "unknown".to_string(),

  2661	                        error: e.to_string(),

  2669	                    // Explicitly transition to LOGGING to recover.
  2670	                    self.set_state(WorkerState::Logging)?;
  2671	                    Err(anyhow::anyhow!("handler failed: {}", e))
  2672	                }
  2673	                Err(_) => {
  2674	                    // Timeout after 60 seconds - attempt best-effort release and transition to LOGGING.
  2675	                    tracing::error!(
  2676	                        bead_id = %bead.id,
  2677	                        "outcome handler timed out after 60s, attempting best-effort release and transitioning to LOGGING"
  2678	                    );
  2679	                    // Set cancellation flag to stop heartbeat and abort any in-flight br calls.
  2680	                    cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);
  2681	                    // Abort the heartbeat task to prevent it from continuing in the background.
  2682	                    heartbeat_task.abort();

  2684	                    let _ = telemetry_clone.emit_try_lock(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {

  2686	                        outcome: "unknown".to_string(),
  2687	                        operation: "handle".to_string(),
  2688	                        error: "timeout after 60s".to_string(),
  2689	                    });
  2690	                    // Attempt best-effort release with timeout.
  2691	                    let _ = tokio::time::timeout(
  2692	                        std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
  2693	                        store_clone.release(&bead_id_clone),
  2694	                    )
  2695	                    .await;
  2696	                    // Explicitly transition to LOGGING to recover.
  2697	                    self.set_state(WorkerState::Logging)?;
  2698	                    Err(anyhow::anyhow!("handler timed out after 60s"))
  2699	                }
  2700	            }
  2701	        }
  2702	        .instrument(outcome_span);
  2703	
  2704	        // The watchdog thread above covers a genuinely wedged runtime. Keep the
  2705	        // 90-second async safety net cancellable so a successful handler does
  2706	        // not leave a sleeping blocking task that delays runtime shutdown.
  2707	        let timeout = tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(90));
  2708	        tokio::pin!(timeout);
  2709	
  2710	        // Use tokio::select! to race between the handling future and the timeout signal.
  2711	        let handler_result = tokio::select! {
  2712	            result = handling_future => {
  2713	                // Handling completed (or inner timeout fired) - cancel the outer timeout.
  2714	                cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);

  2716	                // send() to fail, effectively cancelling it.

  2718	                    Ok(result) => {
  2719	                        heartbeat_task.abort();
  2720	                        result
  2721	                    }
  2722	                    Err(_) => {
  2723	                        // HANDLING failed but recovered - stop heartbeat and continue to LOGGING.
  2724	                        heartbeat_task.abort();
  2725	                        return Ok(());
  2726	                    }
  2727	                }
  2728	            }
  2729	            _ = &mut timeout => {
  2730	                // Outer timeout fired after 90 seconds - this is a critical failure.
  2731	                tracing::error!(
  2732	                    bead_id = %bead.id,
  2733	                    "HANDLING state timed out after 90s, forcing recovery"
  2734	                );
  2735	                // Set cancellation flag to stop all async operations.
  2736	                cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);
  2737	                heartbeat_task.abort();
  2738	                // Emit critical timeout event.
  2739	                let _ = telemetry_clone.emit_try_lock(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {
  2740	                    bead_id: bead_id_clone.clone(),
  2741	                    outcome: "unknown".to_string(),
  2742	                    operation: "handling_state".to_string(),
  2743	                    error: "critical timeout after 90s".to_string(),
  2744	                });
  2745	                // Attempt best-effort release with timeout.
  2746	                let _ = tokio::time::timeout(
  2747	                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
  2748	                    store_clone.release(&bead_id_clone),
  2749	                )
  2750	                .await;
  2751	                // Force transition to LOGGING to recover.
  2752	                self.set_state(WorkerState::Logging)?;

//! Outcome routing: map agent exit codes to explicit handlers.
//!
//! Every possible exit code has a named handler. The type system enforces
//! exhaustiveness — if an outcome can happen, it must have a handler.
//!
//! Depends on: `types`, `config`, `bead_store`, `telemetry`, `validation`.

use std::fmt;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;

use anyhow::Result;
use chrono::Utc;

use crate::bead_store::{BeadStore, SyncRecoveryError};
use crate::config::Config;
use crate::telemetry::{EventKind, Telemetry};
#[cfg(test)]
use crate::types::BeadStatus;
use crate::types::{AgentOutcome, Bead, BeadAction, HandlerResult, Outcome};
use crate::validation::{verify_shipped_work, GateConfig, GateReport, ValidationGate};

// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// classify (convenience re-export)
// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Classify an agent result into an `Outcome`, with verification and shutdown
/// signal support.
///
/// Interruption takes precedence. Otherwise, failed verification is always a
/// failure; only verified results are delegated to the exit-code classifier.
pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool, verified: bool) -> Outcome {
    if was_interrupted {
        return Outcome::Interrupted;
    }

    if !verified {
        return Outcome::Failure;
    }

    Outcome::classify(exit_code, false)
}

// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// OutcomeHandler
// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Routes agent outcomes to their explicit handlers.
pub struct OutcomeHandler {
    config: Config,
    telemetry: Telemetry,
}

impl OutcomeHandler {
    pub fn new(config: Config, telemetry: Telemetry) -> Self {
        OutcomeHandler { config, telemetry }
    }

    /// Run a bead store operation with a 30s timeout.
    ///
    /// Returns `Ok(Some(T))` on success, `Ok(None)` on timeout, and `Err(E)` on
    /// other errors. Callers should treat timeout and error as non-fatal — log
    /// and continue rather than blocking the worker in HANDLING state.
    async fn timeout_op<T, F, Fut>(
        &self,
        op: F,
        operation_name: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<T>, anyhow::Error>
    where
        F: FnOnce() -> Fut,
        Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, anyhow::Error>>,
    {
        match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), op()).await {
            Ok(Ok(result)) => Ok(Some(result)),
            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(e),
            Err(_) => {
                tracing::error!(
                    operation = operation_name,
                    "bead store operation timed out after 30s"
                );
                Ok(None)
            }
        }
    }

    /// Release a bead with sync conflict recovery and graceful failure handling.
    ///
    /// Flow:
    /// 1. Run `br sync --flush-only` to push local writes to JSONL first.
    /// 2. Attempt `br update` to release the bead (set status=open, assignee="").
    /// 3. If SYNC_CONFLICT recovery fails, emit `BeadReleaseFailed` and return Ok.
    ///
    /// This method never returns an error — release failures are non-fatal.
    /// The worker can continue processing other beads even if release fails.
    async fn release_bead(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<Vec<EventKind>> {
        let mut events = Vec::new();

        // Step 1: Flush local writes to JSONL before attempting release.
        // Emit heartbeat before br call to track where hang occurs.
        let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted {
            bead_id: Some(bead.id.clone()),
            state: "HANDLING_FLUSH".to_string(),
        });

        match self.timeout_op(|| store.flush(), "flush").await {
            Ok(Some(())) => {
                tracing::debug!(
                    bead_id = %bead.id,
                    "flushed local changes to JSONL before release"
                );
                // Emit heartbeat after successful flush.
                let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted {
                    bead_id: Some(bead.id.clone()),
                    state: "HANDLING_FLUSH_DONE".to_string(),
                });
            }
            Ok(None) => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    bead_id = %bead.id,
                    "flush timed out before release, attempting release anyway"
                );
                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {
                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
                    outcome: "release".to_string(),
                    operation: "flush".to_string(),
                    error: "timeout after 30s".to_string(),
                });
            }
            Err(e) => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    bead_id = %bead.id,
                    error = %e,
                    "flush failed before release, attempting release anyway"
                );
                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {
                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
                    outcome: "release".to_string(),
                    operation: "flush".to_string(),
                    error: e.to_string(),
                });
            }
        }

        // Step 2: Attempt release with timeout protection.
        // Emit heartbeat before br release call to track where hang occurs.
        let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted {
            bead_id: Some(bead.id.clone()),
            state: "HANDLING_RELEASE".to_string(),
        });

        let release_result =
            tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.release(&bead.id)).await;

        match release_result {
            Ok(Ok(())) => {
                tracing::debug!(
                    bead_id = %bead.id,
                    "bead released successfully"
                );
                // Emit heartbeat after successful release.
                let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted {
                    bead_id: Some(bead.id.clone()),
                    state: "HANDLING_RELEASE_DONE".to_string(),
                });
                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleased {
                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
                    reason: "release_success".to_string(),
                });
            }
            Ok(Err(e)) => {
                // Release failed (br error, not timeout).
                // Check if this is a SyncRecoveryError (sync recovery was attempted but failed).
                if e.downcast_ref::<SyncRecoveryError>().is_some() {
                    tracing::error!(
                        bead_id = %bead.id,
                        error = %e,
                        "br release failed after SYNC_CONFLICT recovery — \
                         worker will continue (bead may remain assigned)"
                    );
                } else {
                    tracing::error!(
                        bead_id = %bead.id,
                        error = %e,
                        "br release failed — worker will continue (bead may remain assigned)"
                    );
                }
                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed {
                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
                    reason: e.to_string(),
                });
            }
            Err(_) => {
                // Timeout after 30s.
                tracing::error!(
                    bead_id = %bead.id,
                    "br release timed out after 30s — worker will continue (bead may remain assigned)"
                );
                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed {
                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
                    reason: "timeout after 30s".to_string(),
                });
            }
        }

        Ok(events)
    }

    /// Run verification gates for a bead, returning whether all passed.
    ///
    /// This is extracted as a helper so it can be called BEFORE outcome classification.
    /// Verification must determine Success, not just exit code 0.
    async fn run_verification_gates(&self, bead: &Bead) -> Result<(bool, Option<GateReport>)> {
        // Try pluggable gates first, fall back to legacy verification commands.
        let gate_opt = if !self.config.gates.is_empty() {
            // New pluggable gate system. Fill in each command gate's stderr
            // cap from `validation.stderr_cap_bytes` unless the gate already
            // set its own override — see GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#9.
            let default_stderr_cap = self.config.validation.stderr_cap_bytes;
            let gate_configs: Vec<(String, GateConfig)> = self
                .config
                .gates
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(i, config)| {
                    let mut config = config.clone();
                    let GateConfig::Command {
                        stderr_cap_bytes, ..
                    } = &mut config;
                    if stderr_cap_bytes.is_none() {
                        *stderr_cap_bytes = Some(default_stderr_cap);
                    }
                    (format!("gate_{}", i), config)
                })
                .collect();
            ValidationGate::new(gate_configs, bead.workspace.clone())
        } else if !self.config.verification.is_empty() {
            // Legacy verification command format.
            ValidationGate::from_commands_with_stderr_cap(
                self.config.verification.clone(),
                bead.workspace.clone(),
                self.config.validation.stderr_cap_bytes,
            )
        } else {
            // No gates configured — treat as verified (backward compatible).
            return Ok((true, None));
        };

        // Run the gate and return the result.
        let gate = gate_opt.ok_or_else(|| {
            anyhow::anyhow!("validation gate creation failed - all gates failed to initialize")
        })?;
        let report = gate.run(bead).await?;
        let all_passed = report.all_passed;
        Ok((all_passed, Some(report)))
    }

    ///
    /// CRITICAL: For exit code 0, verification gates run BEFORE classification.
    /// This ensures Success means verification passed, not just that the agent exited 0.

  2676	                        bead_id = %bead.id,
  2677	                        "outcome handler timed out after 60s, attempting best-effort release and transitioning to LOGGING"
  2678	                    );
  2679	                    // Set cancellation flag to stop heartbeat and abort any in-flight br calls.
  2680	                    cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);
  2681	                    // Abort the heartbeat task to prevent it from continuing in the background.
  2682	                    heartbeat_task.abort();
  2683	                    // Use emit_try_lock() to avoid blocking on telemetry mutex if writer is stuck.
  2684	                    let _ = telemetry_clone.emit_try_lock(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {
  2685	                        bead_id: bead_id_clone.clone(),
  2686	                        outcome: "unknown".to_string(),
  2687	                        operation: "handle".to_string(),
  2688	                        error: "timeout after 60s".to_string(),
  2689	                    });
  2690	                    // Attempt best-effort release with timeout.
  2691	                    let _ = tokio::time::timeout(
  2692	                        std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
  2693	                        store_clone.release(&bead_id_clone),
  2694	                    )
  2695	                    .await;
  2696	                    // Explicitly transition to LOGGING to recover.
  2697	                    self.set_state(WorkerState::Logging)?;
  2698	                    Err(anyhow::anyhow!("handler timed out after 60s"))
  2699	                }
  2700	            }
  2701	        }
  2702	        .instrument(outcome_span);
  2703	
  2704	        // The watchdog thread above covers a genuinely wedged runtime. Keep the
  2705	        // 90-second async safety net cancellable so a successful handler does
  2706	        // not leave a sleeping blocking task that delays runtime shutdown.
  2707	        let timeout = tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(90));
  2708	        tokio::pin!(timeout);
  2709	
  2710	        // Use tokio::select! to race between the handling future and the timeout signal.
  2711	        let handler_result = tokio::select! {
  2712	            result = handling_future => {
  2713	                // Handling completed (or inner timeout fired) - cancel the outer timeout.
  2714	                cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);
  2715	                // The timeout_tx is dropped here, which will cause the blocking thread's
  2716	                // send() to fail, effectively cancelling it.
  2717	                match result {
  2718	                    Ok(result) => {
  2719	                        heartbeat_task.abort();
  2720	                        result
  2721	                    }
  2722	                    Err(_) => {
  2723	                        // HANDLING failed but recovered - stop heartbeat and continue to LOGGING.
  2724	                        heartbeat_task.abort();
  2725	                        return Ok(());
  2726	                    }
  2727	                }
  2728	            }
  2729	            _ = &mut timeout => {
  2730	                // Outer timeout fired after 90 seconds - this is a critical failure.
  2731	                tracing::error!(
  2732	                    bead_id = %bead.id,
  2733	                    "HANDLING state timed out after 90s, forcing recovery"
  2734	                );
  2735	                // Set cancellation flag to stop all async operations.
  2736	                cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);
  2737	                heartbeat_task.abort();
  2738	                // Emit critical timeout event.
  2739	                let _ = telemetry_clone.emit_try_lock(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {
  2740	                    bead_id: bead_id_clone.clone(),
  2741	                    outcome: "unknown".to_string(),
  2742	                    operation: "handling_state".to_string(),
  2743	                    error: "critical timeout after 90s".to_string(),
  2744	                });
  2745	                // Attempt best-effort release with timeout.
  2746	                let _ = tokio::time::timeout(
  2747	                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
  2748	                    store_clone.release(&bead_id_clone),
  2749	                )
  2750	                .await;
  2751	                // Force transition to LOGGING to recover.
  2752	                self.set_state(WorkerState::Logging)?;
  2753	                return Ok(());
  2754	            }
  2755	        };
  2756	
  2757	        // Check if the watchdog triggered during HANDLING state.
  2758	        // This can happen if the heartbeat task detected the watchdog trigger and
  2759	        // set the cancelled flag, or if the watchdog thread set the flag directly.
  2760	        if self.watchdog_triggered.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
  2761	            tracing::error!(
  2762	                bead_id = %bead.id,
  2763	                "watchdog detected during HANDLING state, forcing recovery to LOGGING"
  2764	            );
  2765	            // Clear the watchdog trigger.
  2766	            self.watchdog_triggered.store(false, Ordering::Release);
  2767	            self.handling_state_entered_at = None;
  2768	            // Emit critical timeout event.
  2769	            let _ = self
  2770	                .telemetry
  2771	                .emit_try_lock(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {
  2772	                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
  2773	                    outcome: "unknown".to_string(),
  2774	                    operation: "watchdog".to_string(),
  2775	                    error: format!(
  2776	                        "HANDLING state exceeded {}s timeout",
  2777	                        HANDLING_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_SECS
  2778	                    ),
  2779	                });
  2780	            // Force transition to LOGGING to recover.
  2781	            self.set_state(WorkerState::Logging)?;
  2782	            // Stop the heartbeat task.
  2783	            cancelled.store(true, Ordering::Release);
  2784	            heartbeat_task.abort();
  2785	            return Ok(());
  2786	        }
  2787	
  2788	        // HOOP Hook 2 (event tap): emit the outcome as a single terminal
  2789	        // event on the bead. Best-effort — see hoop_hooks module docs.
  2790	        {
  2791	            let duration_ms = self
  2792	                .exec_started_at
  2793	                .take()
  2794	                .map(|start| start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64);
  2795	            let outcome_str = handler_result.outcome.as_str();
   220	                .config
   221	                .gates
   222	                .iter()
   223	                .enumerate()
   224	                .map(|(i, config)| {
   225	                    let mut config = config.clone();
   226	                    let GateConfig::Command {
   227	                        stderr_cap_bytes, ..
   228	                    } = &mut config;
   229	                    if stderr_cap_bytes.is_none() {
   230	                        *stderr_cap_bytes = Some(default_stderr_cap);
   231	                    }
   232	                    (format!("gate_{}", i), config)
   233	                })
   234	                .collect();
   235	            ValidationGate::new(gate_configs, bead.workspace.clone())
   236	        } else if !self.config.verification.is_empty() {
   237	            // Legacy verification command format.
   238	            ValidationGate::from_commands_with_stderr_cap(
   239	                self.config.verification.clone(),
   240	                bead.workspace.clone(),
   241	                self.config.validation.stderr_cap_bytes,
   242	            )
   243	        } else {
   244	            // No gates configured — treat as verified (backward compatible).
   245	            return Ok((true, None));
   246	        };
   247	
   248	        // Run the gate and return the result.
   249	        let gate = gate_opt.ok_or_else(|| {
   250	            anyhow::anyhow!("validation gate creation failed - all gates failed to initialize")
   251	        })?;
   252	        let report = gate.run(bead).await?;
   253	        let all_passed = report.all_passed;
   254	        Ok((all_passed, Some(report)))
   255	    }
   256	
   257	    /// Handle a process output for the given bead.
   258	    ///
   259	    /// CRITICAL: For exit code 0, verification gates run BEFORE classification.
   260	    /// This ensures Success means verification passed, not just that the agent exited 0.
   261	    /// An agent that exits 0 but fails verification produces Failure, not Success.
   262	    #[tracing::instrument(
   263	        name = "bead.outcome",
   264	        skip(self, store, bead, output),
   265	        fields(
   266	            needle.bead.id = %bead.id,
   267	            needle.outcome = tracing::field::Empty,
   268	            needle.outcome.action = tracing::field::Empty,
   269	        )
   270	    )]
   271	    pub async fn handle(
   272	        &self,
   273	        store: &dyn BeadStore,
   274	        bead: &Bead,
   275	        output: &AgentOutcome,
   276	        was_interrupted: bool,
   277	    ) -> Result<HandlerResult> {
   278	        // For exit code 0, run verification BEFORE classification.
   279	        // This is the core fix: Success must mean verification passed.
   280	        let (verified, gate_report) = if output.exit_code == 0 && !was_interrupted {
   281	            self.run_verification_gates(bead).await?
   282	        } else {
   283	            // Non-zero exit or interrupted — verification irrelevant.
   284	            (true, None)
   285	        };
   286	
   287	        let outcome = classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted, verified);
   288	
   289	        // Set outcome as span attribute
   290	        tracing::Span::current().record("needle.outcome", outcome.as_str());
   291	
   292	        tracing::info!(
   293	            bead_id = %bead.id,
   294	            exit_code = output.exit_code,
   295	            verified,
   296	            outcome = %outcome,
   297	            "handling agent outcome"
   298	        );
   299	
   300	        // Use emit_try_lock() to avoid blocking if telemetry writer is stuck.
   301	        // This prevents worker hang in HANDLING state when telemetry is wedged.
   302	        let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::OutcomeClassified {
   303	            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
   304	            outcome: outcome.as_str().to_string(),
   305	            exit_code: output.exit_code,
   306	        });
   307	
   308	        let (bead_action, telemetry_events) = match outcome.clone() {
   309	            Outcome::Success => self.handle_success(store, bead, gate_report).await?,
   310	            Outcome::Failure => {
   311	                // If we have a gate report with failures, handle as gate failure.
   312	                if let Some(report) = gate_report {
   313	                    if !report.all_passed {
   314	                        self.handle_gate_failure(store, bead, &report).await?
   315	                    } else {
   316	                        self.handle_failure(store, bead).await?
   317	                    }
   318	                } else {
   319	                    self.handle_failure(store, bead).await?
   320	                }
   321	            }
   322	            Outcome::Timeout => self.handle_timeout(store, bead).await?,
   323	            Outcome::AgentNotFound => self.handle_agent_not_found(store, bead).await?,
   324	            Outcome::Interrupted => self.handle_interrupted(store, bead).await?,
   325	            Outcome::Crash(code) => self.handle_crash(store, bead, code).await?,
   326	        };
   327	
   328	        // Emit sub-handler events (e.g. BeadCompleted, BeadOrphaned) to the
   329	        // telemetry sink so they appear in the JSONL log.
   330	        // Use emit_try_lock() to avoid blocking if telemetry writer is stuck.
   331	        for event in &telemetry_events {
   332	            let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(event.clone());
   333	        }
   334	
   335	        // Use emit_try_lock() to avoid blocking if telemetry writer is stuck.
   336	        let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::OutcomeHandled {
   337	            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
   338	            outcome: outcome.as_str().to_string(),
   339	            action: bead_action.to_string(),
   340	        });
   341	
   342	        // Set action as span attribute
   343	        tracing::Span::current().record("needle.outcome.action", bead_action.to_string());
   344	
   345	        // Set span status: Ok for success, Error otherwise
   346	        if !matches!(outcome, Outcome::Success) {
   347	            tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_code", 2u64);
   348	            tracing::Span::current().record("otel.status_description", outcome.as_str());
   349	        }
   350	
   351	        Ok(HandlerResult {
   352	            outcome,
   353	            bead_action,
   354	            telemetry_events,
   355	        })
   356	    }
   357	
   358	    /// Handle a process output with cancellation support.
   359	    ///
   360	    /// Checks the cancellation flag before starting the handler and returns
   361	    /// early if the handler has been cancelled (e.g., due to a timeout in
   362	    /// the worker). This prevents the handler from making further br calls
   363	    /// after a timeout has occurred.
   364	    pub async fn handle_with_cancellation(
   365	        &self,
   366	        store: &dyn BeadStore,
   367	        bead: &Bead,
   368	        output: &AgentOutcome,
   369	        was_interrupted: bool,
   370	        cancelled: Arc<AtomicBool>,
   371	    ) -> Result<HandlerResult> {
   372	        // Check if we've been cancelled before starting.
   373	        if cancelled.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
   374	            tracing::warn!(
   375	                bead_id = %bead.id,
   376	                "outcome handler cancelled before starting, returning early"
   377	            );
   378	            // Return a default HandlerResult to allow the worker to recover.
   379	            // Verification never ran, so conservatively treat as unverified.
   380	            return Ok(HandlerResult {
   381	                outcome: classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted, false),
   382	                bead_action: BeadAction::None,
   383	                telemetry_events: vec![],
   384	            });
   385	        }
   386	
   387	        // Wrap the handler in a timeout to prevent indefinite hangs.
   388	        // This is a safety net in case the internal br call timeouts don't work.
   389	        // Configurable via `validation.outcome_timeout_seconds` (default 50) —
   390	        // see GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#8: a gate running a real verification
   391	        // workload (container test suite, secret scan, fresh-model diff verifier)
   392	        // needs minutes, not seconds.
   393	        let bead_id = bead.id.clone();
   394	        let telemetry = self.telemetry.clone();
   395	        let timeout_secs = self.config.validation.outcome_timeout_seconds;
   396	
   397	        match tokio::time::timeout(
   398	            std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs),
   399	            self.handle(store, bead, output, was_interrupted),
   400	        )
   401	        .await
   402	        {
   403	            Ok(Ok(result)) => Ok(result),
   404	            Ok(Err(e)) => {
   405	                // Handler returned an error.
   406	                tracing::error!(
   407	                    bead_id = %bead_id,
   408	                    error = %e,
   409	                    "outcome handler returned error"
   410	                );
   411	                Err(e)
   412	            }
   413	            Err(_) => {
   414	                // Timeout after `timeout_secs` seconds.
   415	                tracing::error!(
   416	                    bead_id = %bead_id,
   417	                    timeout_secs,
   418	                    "outcome handler timed out, returning early to allow worker recovery"
   419	                );
   420	                // Emit a timeout event for observability.
   421	                let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {
   422	                    bead_id: bead_id.clone(),
   423	                    outcome: classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted, false)
   424	                        .as_str()
   425	                        .to_string(),
   426	                    operation: "handle".to_string(),
   427	                    error: format!("timeout after {}s", timeout_secs),
   428	                });
   429	                // Return a default HandlerResult to allow the worker to recover.
   430	                // The worker's 60-second timeout wrapper will handle best-effort release.
   431	                // Verification never ran, so conservatively treat as unverified.
   432	                Ok(HandlerResult {
   433	                    outcome: classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted, false),
   434	                    bead_action: BeadAction::Released,
   435	                    telemetry_events: vec![EventKind::BeadReleased {
   436	                        bead_id,
   437	                        reason: "handler_timeout".to_string(),
   438	                    }],
   439	                })
   440	            }
   441	        }
   442	    }
   443	
   444	    /// Success: verification already passed, now verify bead closure.
   445	    ///
   446	    /// CRITICAL: This is only called when verification PASSED.
   447	    /// If verification failed, classification produces Failure and handle_failure
   448	    /// is called instead. This ensures Success means verification passed.
   449	    ///
   450	    /// Flow:
   451	    /// 1. If gates ran, emit VerificationPassed telemetry.
   452	    /// 2. Check if agent closed the bead.
   453	    ///    - Closed → emit BeadCompleted.
   454	    ///    - Still open → emit BeadOrphaned warning.
   455	    ///
   456	    /// NEEDLE does NOT auto-close — the agent owns closure via `br close`.
   457	    async fn handle_success(
   458	        &self,
   459	        store: &dyn BeadStore,
   460	        bead: &Bead,
   461	        gate_report: Option<GateReport>,
   462	    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {
   463	        tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, "agent completed successfully");
   464	
   465	        // If gates ran and passed, emit telemetry.
   466	        if let Some(report) = gate_report {
   467	            let gates_run = report.results.len() as u32;
   468	            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::VerificationPassed {
   469	                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),
   470	                gates_run,
   471	            })?;
   472	            tracing::info!(
   473	                bead_id = %bead.id,
   474	                gates_run,
   475	                "all validation gates passed"
   476	            );
   477	        }
   478	
   479	        // Reset failure count on successful gate completion.
   480	        // This ensures the bead starts fresh on the next cycle if re-claimed.
   481	        let _ = self.reset_failure_count(store, bead).await;
   482	
   483	        // Normal success flow: check if agent closed the bead.
   484	        let mut events = Vec::new();
   485	
   486	        // Use timeout for show() to prevent indefinite hang in HANDLING state.
   487	        match self.timeout_op(|| store.show(&bead.id), "show").await {
   488	            Ok(Some(current)) if current.status.is_done() => {
